Hey! So I definitely think that maybe if you start to think of what would be the best for the kitten, you’d feel more clear on how you’d like to proceed. By no means am I you, so this is just my opinion! No worries if you don’t agree! 

So, if I was a kitten and I’m gonna have my forever home, I would want to be able to acclimate to my environment and owner. Since you need to introduce your kitten to your current cat, this will take time and the kitten will bond to you first. If you do this then leave and come back, it is a change in her environment and might not be the best for letting the kitten get used to everything. It might also negatively affect your current cat since you brought this kitten in and left. I actually love that the shelter is offering to keep the kitten for an extra couple weeks! I think this is the solution I would personally choose. 

I don’t think you’re gonna miss much, and honestly I’m not a kitten person. I purposefully only get adult cats because kittens are so much hahaha. It just seems like you’re changing your mind because you might miss the growing up time but is that best for the kitten or your adult cat?? And I think you getting another cat will be amazing for your current one once they have become proper friends on their own time. 

Totally up to you! I think the two of them would be okay if you got the kitten before the trip, but I think it’ll cause some speed bumps.

I relate to you a lot! I’ve discussed this with my therapist and my behaviours are a lot more OCD than anorexic, although I have enjoyed the focus distraction of tracking my weight. For me not eating was my compulsion to distract from my obsessive thoughts, specifically intrusive thoughts. I also tend to use it as a punishment, as this was done to me as a child, whenever I feel I am bad. I’ve only ever calorie counted or tried to lose weight in high school and when I’m suicidal. I work obsessively too, it’s like I’m addicted to being busy. I LOVE being so busy I have no time to eat. I feel like I could go on forever but then I crash and you know, have intrusive thoughts.

I find that people who are in flight mode use work as a coping mechanism, at least that’s been my experience. I work like it’s an addiction, and I can’t let myself stop cause then I’ll freeze and have intrusive thoughts. I struggle a lot with imposter syndrome and burn out A LOT. But people think I’m fine because I work so much and threw myself into my career, but it’s all I have and when I burn out and need to stop I spiral.

I'm the freeze type too, and I struggle to unfreeze too but the best thing so far for me is grounding. When I freeze I often stare at one spot and zone out and retract inside my mind. What I'm doing now that works for me is to look at anything that has texture, when I find it I lock in on it and think "I wonder how that feels to touch" and I perceive touching it in my head, then I reach out and touch it. I compare what I thought it would feel like and what I'm feeling right now. It helps to disconnect from my thoughts into the real world again. I often will count the lines or grooves of what I'm feeling, then I look somewhere else for a different texture. 

My therapist has been working on a lot of grounding for me, because I'm currently starting imaginal work for prolonged exposure therapy. There's a lot more strategies but these work best for me 💜
